name: strong-windows-qemu-whpx

status.operational_gate: C6: not operational until F-03.3.1, F-03.3.2, F-03.4 and S-02.x pass, cited by property id.
status.provider_validation: PASS, 2026-11-06 (F-03.2.1b, evidence/F-03.2.1b-provider-validation.md): the paused boot (-S) with the full launch.argv answered QMP in prelaunch with 8 CPUs and 16 GiB, and quit exited 0. Observed warnings: -mon is deprecated; 'Ignoring request for interrupt vector 0' (open items for F-03.2.2 in README.md). Re-validated 2026-11-06 (F-03.2.2a, evidence/F-03.2.2a-seed-and-monitor.md) after -mon was replaced by -object monitor-qmp: the paused boot with a generated seed.iso answered QMP in prelaunch with enabled whpx, query-block listed root, scratch and seed (seed and base read-only), quit exited 0, and no deprecation warning was printed; 'Ignoring request for interrupt vector 0' recurred.
status.guest_validation: Observed 2026-11-06 (F-03.2.2b, evidence/F-03.2.2b-guest-lifecycle.md), under the Owner's guest-validation authorization (decision 0003). Two disposable guests (f0322b-a, f0322b-b) were created with tools/guest.py, booted under enabled whpx, ready in 9.7 s, then stopped and destroyed; the instance directories are gone and the image and QEMU pins are unchanged. The F-03.2 proof (declared versus observed) has no mismatch: 8 vCPU, MemTotal 16382796 kB of 16 GiB, 40 and 120 GiB disks, seed and base read-only, no vmx/svm in guest /proc/cpuinfo, cloud-init accepted the seed (DataSourceNoCloud [seed=/dev/vdc]), machine-ids differ (systemd generated them at first boot), user agent without sudo, and root SSH refused. SSH and QMP listened on 127.0.0.1 only; the LAN address and ::1 refused the forwarded ports. Every guest egress probe was blocked, with positive controls passing, but off-link destinations failed in the guest for lack of a default route, so SLIRP restrict=on was exercised only for 10.0.2.2 and 10.0.2.3 (F-03.3.2). inspect P6 FAILs on the contract's literal /tmp/.X11-unix check: the guest's systemd tmpfiles create an empty directory there. 'Ignoring request for interrupt vector 0' printed once at each launch and the guest ran normally. Guest kernel warning: 'x86/fpu: misordered xstate at 1408' under -cpu max. Evidence toward F-03.3.x and F-03.4 only; not operational (C6).

host.host_principal: The Owner's Windows account. QEMU runs as an ordinary user process: no service, no elevation, no installer. The strong tier buys a kernel boundary, not a principal boundary (profiles P8).

provider.name: qemu
provider.install_method: A2: tools/msys2_lock.py install downloads the locked MSYS2 packages, checks each sha256, validates every archive entry (the built-in tar.exe decodes them), writes regular files only under {qemu_prefix} (hardlinks materialised as copies) and verifies every installed file. No installer, no administrator rights, no registry or PATH change.
provider.whpx_in_build: MSYS2's qemu-common documentation (share/doc/qemu/msys2.readme.txt) shows '-accel whpx'; the pinned qemu-system-x86_64.exe contains the WHPX accelerator's messages, including 'WHPX: No accelerator found'. Runtime availability: observed on this host in F-03.2.1b (evidence/F-03.2.1b-provider-validation.md): -accel help lists whpx, and in the paused boot QMP query-accelerators reported {"enabled": "whpx"}. Inference: the WHPX partition and its vCPUs were set up without error, since QEMU stayed up, answered QMP and printed no WHPX: line.

accelerator.name: whpx
accelerator.reason: QEMU uses TCG when no -accel is given, and tries each listed accelerator in turn (qemu.org invocation, -accel). Exactly one -accel whpx, and no accel= on -machine, makes a missing WHPX a launch failure that the harness reports as TIER_UNAVAILABLE naming A1.

state_dir.rules: Named explicitly by the Owner on every invocation (contract section 11): outside the checkout, outside %USERPROFILE%, no comma (QEMU option syntax). Nothing in it is committed.

signature.evidence: https://cloud.debian.org/images/cloud/ states that for the current images 'the safest method is to download the image and checksum files over TLS from cloud.debian.org or cdimage.debian.org'; only the legacy OpenStack images carry SHA512SUMS.sign. The same SHA512SUMS was fetched from both hosts and was identical; the image's JSON manifest carries the same sha512.

image.check_before_launch: sha256 of the local file, immediately before every launch; a mismatch refuses the launch (profiles P9).

firmware.type: SeaBIOS (bios-256k.bin as shipped in the pinned QEMU package)
firmware.reason: The image boots by BIOS or UEFI (it ships grub-pc-bin and grub-efi-amd64). BIOS needs no per-instance writable firmware variable store. Other data files QEMU may load (ACPI and option ROMs) come from the same pinned package; the virtio-net option ROM is disabled (romfile=).

kernel.reason: The image's own bootloader and kernel boot; they are covered by the image digest.

generator.status: implemented and tested in F-03.2.2a; observed in F-03.2.2b: the Debian guest's cloud-init 25.1.4 accepted the volume (DataSourceNoCloud [seed=/dev/vdc], status done, no errors) on two instances

seed.record_at_create: sha256 of seed.iso in the launch record; the same inputs give the same digest.

profile_revision.record_at_create: git rev-parse HEAD of the checkout; create refuses when profiles/ has uncommitted changes.

ceilings.justification: Host: 32 logical CPUs, 62 GB RAM, about 750 GB free on D:. One guest takes 25 % of the logical CPUs and 16 GiB (about 26 % of RAM), leaving 24 CPUs and about 46 GB for Windows and the Owner's WSL VM (whose default ceiling is half of RAM). Disks are thin qcow2: an instance can grow to at most 160 GiB, so the state directory holds four instances at full allocation. Two instances at full memory beside a fully used WSL VM would overcommit RAM; the reference mode is one shared instance. These are the outer caps for decision 0001's per-conversation overrides; Moby's caps (F-04.1) sit inside them.

nested_virt_masking: -cpu max,vmx=off,svm=off. Observed at the configuration level in F-03.2.1b (evidence/F-03.2.1b-provider-validation.md): WHPX accepted the max model with these flags off; QOM vmx and svm are false on all 8 vCPUs, and filtered-features is all zero. Unobserved until F-03.2.2: the guest-visible CPUID; inside the guest, grep -c -E 'vmx|svm' /proc/cpuinfo must be 0.

guest_agent.reason: Management is SSH over the loopback forward. No virtio-serial device, so no QEMU guest agent channel (profiles P6).

network.posture: restrict=on: the guest cannot reach the host or the outside except through the explicit forwards below (qemu.org invocation: restrict=on 'does not affect any explicitly set forwarding rules').
network.enforcement_point: QEMU SLIRP restrict=on, with guestfwd to host-side endpoints for inference and provision: candidate; qualified by F-03.3.2.

endpoints.purpose: QMP (lifecycle and inspect); host-side only, not reachable from the guest
git bundle transfer by SFTP over the management SSH forward

endpoints.mechanism: guestfwd to a host-side allowlisting proxy

network.port_allocation: {ssh_port} and {qmp_port} are free ports on 127.0.0.1 chosen at create and kept in the launch record.
network.local_exposure: Loopback ports are reachable by any local process of any user on the host; disclosed, not prevented (Python's standard library has no AF_UNIX socket on Windows, so QMP uses loopback TCP).

identity.ssh_key: ed25519, generated at create with Windows' built-in OpenSSH ssh-keygen into {instance_dir}/ssh/; never ~/.ssh.
identity.host_key_trust: Fingerprints read from cloud-init's block on the serial log ({instance_dir}/serial.log), written to {instance_dir}/ssh/known_hosts.
identity.machine_id: Generated by the guest's systemd at first boot of a fresh overlay; uniqueness observed in F-03.2.2.

bindings.preflight: Read-only capability report: OS and arch; state directory named, existing, outside the checkout and %USERPROFILE%; provider binaries match their sha256; 'qemu-system-x86_64 -accel help' lists whpx; the image file matches its sha256. Each failure names its Owner act (A1, A2, A3).
bindings.create: Refuse if {instance_dir} exists. Create it; generate the SSH key; check the image sha256; qemu-img create the root overlay (40 GiB, backing the pinned image) and the scratch disk (120 GiB); generate seed.iso; allocate ports; write launch.json (every boot input with its digest, the argv, the profile revision); launch QEMU detached.
bindings.start: Relaunch from launch.json after re-checking every digest in it.
bindings.stop: QMP system_powerdown; after stop_timeout_s, QMP quit; if the process still runs, terminate that process id only.
bindings.destroy: Stop with force if running, then delete {instance_dir} only. Absent: succeed and report absent. The image, the provider and every other path are untouched.
bindings.recreate: destroy, then create with the same name and profile.
bindings.inspect: QMP query-version, query-cpus-fast, query-memory-size-summary, query-block, query-pci, query-chardev; qemu-img info of root and scratch; guest probes over SSH per profiles P1-P12; labelled per profiles P11.
bindings.exec: ssh with identity.ssh_client_options to agent@127.0.0.1 -p {ssh_port}. Operator and provisioning only; never offered to agents.
bindings.exchange push: A git bundle of a bounded snapshot, copied by SFTP into /home/agent/exchange.
bindings.exchange pull: A git bundle and evidence copied by SFTP into a harness-owned staging directory under {state_dir}; never into the Owner's repositories.

launch.notes: QMP is the one monitor, created with -object monitor-qmp on the loopback socket chardev (QEMU 11.1 deprecates -mon). No USB controller, audio device, display, VGA, monitor (HMP), file share, 9p, SMB or virtio-serial device is created: -nodefaults removes the defaults and none is added. The root overlay's backing node is bound explicitly to the pinned image, so the overlay header's backing path is not trusted.
